rubric.baseline: Original audit identifies a useful local MCP hub niche; independent retention evidence is not yet retained.
criteria: Ten independent weekly users for eight elapsed weeks; report all enrollment, drop-off, missing and weekly activity denominators.
At least eight of ten target novices complete a first model-plus-MCP run in <=15 minutes without coding or live coaching.
Independent users record repeated MCP hub/debugger/agent workflows and benefits; stars and bots cannot satisfy adoption.

rubric.baseline: Advertised breadth exists; #517 local fixes and published observations differ, and #526 lacks full 128-tool release confirmation.
criteria: Installed-artifact matrix retains all advertised model, MCP tool/resource/prompt/App, graph/branch/loop/subflow, debugger, HITL, automation, /v1 and proxy journeys.
Reach all 128 tools in the #526 fixture, preserve arguments during same-server discovery, and never invoke before Test.
Record supported platform/install/provider/tool failures and prerequisites; passing fixture coverage alone is insufficient.

rubric.baseline: Exact-source verify run reports success; effective-main rules were reported inactive in the plan; enforcement and distribution acceptance are pending.
criteria: Require review and meaningful root/MCP typecheck, lint, ordinary/isolated tests, API inventory, Windows/Linux builds and packed process smoke on the selected release SHA.
Verify npm/container/installer provenance, migration requirements and retained raw checksums; a version string cannot substitute for source correspondence.
Accountable human owners execute vulnerability response and disposable release drills.

rubric.baseline: Backend/shared/frontend split exists with complex execution/MCP modules; independent maintainability demonstration is pending.
criteria: Version module ownership and execution/MCP contracts; enforce prohibited imports and use behavior-preserving incremental refactors.
A second human diagnoses and changes a core execution/MCP path using onboarding guidance and passing boundary checks.
No new critical/high regression in claimed profiles; evidence records change scope and exact revision.

rubric.baseline: Local-first is a trust boundary, not host MCP confinement; owner ingress, migration, safe transfer and enforced isolation remain acceptance work.
criteria: Authenticated owner sessions and scoped API/MCP ingress reject every declared unauthorized matrix case, including CSRF and account/workspace confusion.
Private credential migration round-trips verified disposable legacy records; tampered/unknown/cross-owner transfers fail closed with no plaintext leakage.
Independent threat-model review has zero unresolved high/critical findings; OS/container enforcement, not scanner scores, bounds declared MCP capabilities.

rubric.baseline: The #520 controlled regression detects two fixed defects but does not replay the original live OOM workload. Persona automated passes coexist with manual/live gates.
criteria: Retain #520 negative control and confirm the original workload on the installed release; byte/concurrency/archive/event budgets fail safely before unbounded allocation.
Run declared interactive and persistent-worker failure/recovery matrix; zero lost accepted work or duplicate external effects, with uncertain effects retained for observation.
Full exact-revision offline Persona soak and validator satisfy unchanged append/RSS/growth contracts; live and manual acceptance remain separately required.

rubric.baseline: Original audit reports concentration in author/bot commits; no independent continuity or sustained human study is recorded here.
criteria: Two additional humans independently review, perform disposable release/recovery drills and accept backup responsibility.
At least three non-author humans make substantive contributions/reviews across 90 elapsed days.
Record unique human identities, participation windows, missing observations and conflicts; bot activity and promotion do not qualify.

rubric.baseline: project-status preserves the September 16 failed simulation. Later reported passes need release attribution without deleting failures.
criteria: Every support/maturity/security/migration/runtime claim maps to an exact-source/artifact evidence entry and visible scope limits.
README, project-status, changelog and topic-owned architecture/API/security guides agree on claimed profiles, prerequisites, failures and experimental limits.
Historical failures, later automated results, local patches, simulations, live runs and human observations remain distinguishable; independent rubric/reassessment disagreements block closure.

rubric.baseline: Local single-owner remains the present envelope; persistent-worker recovery and multi-user isolation/sharing are separately gated.
criteria: Installed releases pass install/upgrade/backup/restore, crash recovery, resource/health/audit controls on each claimed platform/install profile.
Generation-bound #547 receipts distinguish observed owned-process exit from disconnected state; #553 opts in only proven worker-local schedules while copied schedules stay suppressed.
Shared/public profile passes two-user isolation, credential/process separation, team share/revoke/edit-conflict matrices and independent security review; authentication alone is insufficient.

profiles.label: Local single-owner workbench (current default envelope)
trustBoundaries: One trusted owner, loopback listeners; host MCP code can access host privileges and remote providers receive selected data.
Workspace separation is logical; no claim of multiple-user authorization or sandboxing from local-first defaults.
prerequisites: Node ^22.23.4 || ^24.22.1 for this source baseline; the chosen distribution must declare its own exact runtime identity. Provider credential/subscription/quota or compatible local model; network as selected.
MCP-dependent git/Python/uv/browser/system prerequisites and operator consent; custom encryption protection and migration acceptance.
exclusions: Personas/persistent goals remain experimental outside demonstrated envelope.
Untrusted shared/public access and unattended multi-week claims need their own gates.

profiles.label: Authenticated persistent worker/service
trustBoundaries: Dedicated scoped worker bearer and immutable worker identity separate from owner/browser session.
Snapshot/config data may contain secrets; capture/import require original authority and private credential handling.
Startup recovery admits only proven worker-local eligible schedules; copied snapshot schedules stay suppressed.
prerequisites: Accepted owner/scoped ingress, credential migration, enforced MCP capabilities and resource budgets.
Service health/audit/backup/restore, process receipts and declared OS/provider/tool prerequisites; no live controller activation implied.
exclusions: Sealed cross-stream source fixtures and process death are not spending/replay/cleanup authority.
Autonomy remains experimental pending actual elapsed evidence.

profiles.label: Authenticated isolated shared/public deployment
trustBoundaries: Authenticated principal bound to owner/account/workspace; isolated credentials, processes, storage and exports.
Teams share only explicit versioned permissions with revocation and edit-conflict protection; public ingress requires TLS/proxy/session/API threat-model review.
Original/current request/account identity and uncertainty survive cross-stream adapters; no new replay authority from source acceptance.

methods: hardened pinned container/service with authenticated ingress

prerequisites: #573 architecture decision, #574 Tier 0 isolation, #575 team-sharing acceptance.
Independent security review and installed operator/backup/recovery matrix; OS/install restrictions explicitly accepted by reviewer.
exclusions: No current supported shared/public envelope claimed.
Tier 2 fine-grained roles remain unimplemented beyond accepted contract.
No silent profile reduction; all nine original dimensions stay in scope.
